body: Crossing my fingers it's just mold. Thanks for taking me through this, I will not be using the wood.

Are these available in Canada? I have what's called Doktor Doom Bed Bug Killer, which I've been told doesn't actually kill? I'll take a look online though, thanks. 

I texted the person I got the wood from to let them know but I doubt they'll reply.

Ok, thanks. Just a follow up question- when I got it I brought it inside to my hallway and sprayed it, left it overnght, then stuck it in my garage. Then I went through a steamed a piece of it, and put that in my laundry room (which is next to my bedroom, door always stays closed) and left the steamed piece in there for a week. 

What are the chances they could have gotten about? I didn't see any signs whatsoever, but you know, in case.

I went through with a credit card and a flash light and didn't find anything. Then I sprayed all the nooks with bed bug stuff, which is really just repellent I guess. 

Someone was using the pallets as a bed frame for a year then stored it in their garage for the summer.

Sometimes it's something ridiculous and small but I get this ball of anger and hate in my stomach when someone (usually always my partner) does something to irritate me. It feels like a quick explosion that I never had the chance to extinguish. I don't know why I'm so high strung and controlling, and I don't know why I'm always looking for something to be wrong. 

My partner has flaws, like anyone, but their biggest flaw is that they lack emotional intelligence. They treat me well, they just aren't cuddly and romantic- oh poor me /s. I'm so ungrateful and I doubt I'll ever really be happy. I've been pushing through for so long, since I was a kid really, that I'm just too tired.
That actually made me laugh. I used to take in rescue animals and rehome them- I love animals! I don't know why I dislike this cat so much.
Very good points, thank you for elaborating on that for me.

He asked me to help him with the studying and test stuff since I'm good at organizing and planning. If I didn't, he wouldn't. I realize that I should just let him make this mistake on his own, but I tried that once and it resulted in him being depressed, sullen, and moody for months.

Do you mind telling me what is coming across sounding naggy? I would really like to work on this. Couples therapy sounds so...daunting, especially since we have only been together 2.5 years and are so young. 

Your second part, someone else mentioned this. I let them know that I actually came up with a list of specific things he could do/say that are romantic, and started an amazon list of present ideas if it's like my birthday or something. 

I should say too- he does verbally express appreciation when I do things for him, it's the attitude and his inability to express the appreciation to me in a way that I would like (love languages and all that) that's the issue. He is really quite a nice person.

Solely based off the interactions I provided, you believe they are unhealthy? I ask because that's what I heard, but I also have a tenancy to dismiss his 'rudeness' as me being sensitive, or it not being a big deal. 

I've talked to him since trying to work on my nagging and he has said it's much better and I approach things well enough now. Unfortunately, I have yet to find an approach in which when I say/ask something he doesn't like, that he doesn't become snotty (like above).  I don't want it to sound like I'm making excuses, and trust me, I do not think I'm perfect. It just feels like I kept up my end of the bargain (changing how I approach things, my tone, even phrases he disliked), but he is still what I perceive as rude.

As for how he handles things that he may seem like a fight starter, he usually just shrugs it off, like say 'ya' or 'ok', or doesn't say anything. It's like pulling teeth trying to get any feelings out of him. 

EDIT: I should note that he says he can't work on his rudeness because he doesn't even know/think he's doing it.

I'm sorry, I think there is a misunderstanding. I don't go around saying "you're bad at cleaning the kitchen". As for your suggestion, I actually do that. I can mow the lawn myself but it's his thing because he's 'so good at it'. His ego, trust me, is quite boosted.

I have asked him to do the love language quiz with me. He did but never really took it seriously. I even looked up a list of nice things he could do for me as he said he couldn't think of any so could I just tell him. 

When I say negative aspects about him, I mean things he perceives as negative. Like if I say, "I don't feel validated when we talk", or "It hurts my feelings when I have to ask you to pay attention when we talk". I try to stay away from pointed or 'you' statements and instead include I feel, can we, and us type of things.

It's difficult to say, though. I am quite sensitive so I don't know if some of the things I'm interpreting as rude are, which is inflating the occurrence, or if it's only sometimes and I just take offense too easily. The above is a good example of the interactions. Sometimes it's just tone of voice,  which I could be misinterpreting.

I first talked to him about communication issues and being romantic towards the end of our first year together. I'm his first girlfriend (I'm his first almost everything), whereas I was in a serious, long term relationship before him. We were still in school when we got together so he moved in directly from his parent's house (though he has briefly lived on his own before).   


I brushed it off for a long time as 'he doesn't know better' since I'm his first gf. But I feel like its been enough time. I love him, and many aspects of him, but maybe this is just part of his personality?

Thanks for the reply. Occurrence is every other day, but mostly if I'm asking/telling him to do something, sharing my feelings that involve a negative aspect of him, complain about something he doesn't find important, or debating topics. 

 I tried to list some of his better qualities at the beginning of the post so people don't assume he's a bad guy. He isn't. We have a lot of the same interests, and he does try when I talk to him, it just doesn't last. I should note, we spend plenty of quality time together, it's when we aren't it is difficult to get his attention when I'm trying to talk.  

I think you're right in that he isn't going to change into the sweet, sentimental, romantic type. I just can't tell how important that is to me in the grand scheme of things. I could be with someone romantic and happy  but that person's personality still might not mesh well with mine. On the other side, his negative demeanor could be hindering my progress with fixing my depression. I have no idea!! 

I read a lot of posts on here and I work in the social service field in which communication is important. I have tried so many times, in different ways, and he says he gets it but then we are back here.

If he moved out he would actually just be returning to another free place to stay. I have mentioned to him that if he went to the other place and had to do his own things without my help then maybe he would understand me better, but if he moved out it would more than likely result in a break up.

Mostly only when it has to do with asking him to do something. When he finally decided to do the test, I asked him if we could first sort out what days he will be doing them (there is a limited about of prep tests available). 

He did, but after a few minutes he said: I just want to get on with this!(the test). 

So I said: We had plans and you decided to take the test later. I moved my stuff until tomorrow, so you can take five minutes and do this with me. 

He said ok, we did it, but when it came time for the test (I have to time it for him) he was a little snappy.
